creator: brooke_wrightmode
title: 'i-have-adhd' (ayghri/i-have-adhd): free MIT skill/plugin for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor that forces action-first, numbered, tangent-free answers with no preamble or closers

tools.name: i-have-adhd
tools.detail: GitHub ayghri/i-have-adhd, public, MIT; folders .agents/plugins, .claude-plugin, .codex-plugin, .cursor/skills/i-have-adhd, .github/workflows, evals, hooks, scripts, skills/i-have-adhd, tests; uninstall via 'claude plugin uninstall i-have-adhd' / 'claude plugin marketplace remove ...'

claims: Stops Claude or ChatGPT giving verbose, overwhelming answers and gives only what you need to get started
README: 'A skill for your coding assistant that stops it from burying the answer. Action first. Steps numbered. No "Hope this helps!"'

Ten rules: 1 lead with the next action, 2 number multi-step tasks, 3 end with one concrete next step, 4 suppress tangents, 5 (one action per turn, partly obscured), 6 (partly obscured), 7 make wins visible, 8 matter-of-fact errors, 9 cap lists at 5 items, 10 no preamble, no recap, no closers
how_to_steps: Install from the GitHub repo (INSTALL.md referenced; Claude plugin, Codex plugin and Cursor skill variants present)
Use normally; answers come action-first and numbered
To customize: fork, edit skills/i-have-adhd/SKILL.md, then swap in your copy with 'claude plugin uninstall i-have-adhd' and 'claude plugin marketplace remove ...' before reinstalling
on_screen_only: Title overlay 'If you use AI + have ADHD you NEED this'
GitHub mobile view: 'ayghri / i-have-adhd', Public, Issues 5, branch main, last commit 'ayghri 6 hours ago', README + MIT license

relevance.why: A time-poor founder benefits from terse, next-action-first output; the repo is small, multi-platform (Claude/Codex/Cursor) and comes with evals/tests, which is more than most prompt-style skills. Overlaps with output-style settings and existing terse-output skills.

implement_score.why: Trivial to install or to just paste the 10 rules into CLAUDE.md / a custom output style. Cheap experiment; check it does not suppress explanations needed for review of risky changes (rule 'cap lists at 5' could hide items).
